extra_misconceptions.fact: In Chaturanga and Persian Shatranj, the counselor piece moved only one diagonal square until European reforms around 1475.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The Queen has always been the most powerful piece on the board since the earliest days of Indian Chaturanga.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Castling evolved in 16th-century Europe from the King's leap to speed up piece development and improve King safety.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Castling was part of original 6th-century Indian chess rules to protect the Rajah from central chariot attacks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wilhelm Steinitz became the first official World Champion in 1886, and FIDE began organizing the title match in 1948.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: World Chess Championship titles have been officially awarded by an international federation since the 1500s.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Both the initial two-square pawn advance and the en passant rule were introduced in medieval Europe to speed up play.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The two-square initial pawn advance and en passant capture existed in ancient Sanskrit Chaturanga manuscripts.

extra_socratic_questions: What changes transformed the medieval Ferz and Alfil into the modern Queen and Bishop during the late 15th century?
Which historical rule additions in Renaissance Europe accelerated the opening phase of chess compared to Shatranj?
What specific tournament records or published games verify the historical impact of the Grandmaster you researched?
Where did the 6th-century Indian game of Chaturanga originate before spreading through Persia to the Islamic world?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Repeated draw offers distract the opponent and violate chess etiquette; offer a draw only after making your move and before pressing the clock.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Offering a draw repeatedly while your opponent's clock is running is an acceptable psychological tactic in tournament play.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Strong players combine focused tactical calculation with strategic evaluation of pawn structure, piece activity, and King safety.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Good chess players rely purely on memorizing dozens of moves ahead rather than evaluating positional features on the board.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Greeting your opponent before play and shaking hands afterward are foundational expectations of chess sportsmanship and respect.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Refusing to shake hands before a game starts is a harmless personal preference in rated scholastic tournaments.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Spectators must remain completely silent and never interfere in an active game; only players or the tournament director may intervene.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Spectators watching a live game are allowed to point out illegal moves or time forfeits to the players at the board.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes a long-term strategic plan from a short-term tactical calculation during a competitive chess game?
Under what condition should a player offer a draw so that the request respects proper over-the-board chess etiquette?
Why is it poor sportsmanship to hover your hand over the board or tap pieces while your opponent is calculating?
Which decision-making habit from evaluating candidate moves transfers directly to solving complex academic problems?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Castling is prevented only if the King is in check, passes through check, or lands in check; the Rook may cross an attacked square.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A King cannot castle queenside if the Rook on a1 or a8 is currently under attack or passes through an attacked b-file square.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A promoted pawn may become a Queen, Rook, Bishop, or Knight of the same color regardless of which pieces remain on the board.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A pawn reaching the eighth rank can only be promoted to a piece that has already been captured earlier in the game.

extra_misconceptions.fact: En passant must be executed on the very next turn immediately after the opponent's two-square pawn advance, or the right is lost.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An en passant capture can be played several moves after an enemy pawn advances two squares past your fifth-rank pawn.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Announcing check is never required in formal chess rules, and players must recognize threats to their own King on every turn.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Saying check out loud is mandatory under official rules before a checkmate or capture can be legally enforced on the board.

extra_socratic_questions: Which visual check confirms that the chessboard and both royals are oriented properly before the first move is played?
Under what condition is castling temporarily illegal even if neither the King nor the chosen Rook has previously moved?
What happens to a game immediately when the player whose turn it is to move is not in check and has no legal moves?
Where must the capturing pawn land when executing a legal en passant capture right after an enemy pawn advances two squares?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard algebraic notation uses uppercase K for the King and uppercase N for the Knight to avoid ambiguity on the score sheet.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: In standard algebraic notation, the letter K is used to record Knight moves while King moves are written out in full.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Algebraic notation omits piece letters for pawns, recording only the destination square like e4 or the starting file for captures like exd5.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pawn moves in algebraic notation must always begin with an uppercase P before the destination coordinate, such as Pe4.

extra_misconceptions.fact: In the Queen's Gambit, White offers the c4 pawn temporarily to gain central control and can usually recover the pawn with strong play.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The Queen's Gambit is a true material sacrifice where Black can permanently keep the c4 pawn without positional drawbacks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sound opening play uses only a few central pawn moves so Knights and Bishops can develop rapidly toward the center before castling.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Moving as many pawns as possible in the first six moves is the fastest way to control the board and develop an attack.

extra_socratic_questions: What extra file or rank character is required in algebraic notation when two identical Knights can legally reach the same square?
Why does the King transition from hiding behind a castled pawn shelter in the opening to becoming an active attacker in the endgame?
Which opening principle is violated when a player brings the Queen out on move two to chase unguarded flank pawns?
What exact sequence of moves distinguishes the Ruy Lopez on move three from the Italian Game after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only an absolute pin against the King makes moving illegal; a piece in a relative pin shielding a Queen or Rook may still legally move.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A pinned piece is always legally forbidden from moving off the line of attack regardless of which piece stands behind it.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Because two separate pieces attack the King simultaneously in a double check, a King move is the only legal response.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A double check can be neutralized by capturing the moving piece that just delivered check or by blocking one line of attack.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A King and two Knights cannot force checkmate against a lone King unless the defender blunders into a corner trap.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Two Knights and a King can easily force checkmate from any position against a lone enemy King on an open board.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Effective clock management saves time during familiar opening moves so you have ample minutes for complex middle game critical positions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Spending half of your total clock time on routine opening moves is good clock management because it prevents early mistakes.

extra_socratic_questions: What geometric ordering of the two target pieces distinguishes a tactical pin from a skewer along an open file or diagonal?
Why must the defending King move rather than capture or interpose when placed in a double check by a discovered attack?
What happens to a player stuck in zugzwang during an endgame when every legal move on the board worsens their position?
Where should White reposition a Rook during the two-Rook staircase checkmate when the enemy King approaches to attack it?

extra_misconceptions.fact: In a Swiss system tournament, no player is eliminated; everyone plays every round paired against opponents with similar cumulative scores.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Losing a single round in a Swiss system chess tournament eliminates a player from competing in the remaining scheduled rounds.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Intentionally touching an opponent's piece on your turn obligates you to capture that specific piece if a legal capture exists.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Under the touch-move rule, touching an opponent's piece requires you to move one of your own pieces only if you choose to.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Tournament rules require a player to press the chess clock using the exact same hand that moved the piece on the board.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pressing the chess clock with your free hand while your other hand is still placing a piece on its square is legal.

extra_misconceptions.fact: If a player runs out of time when the opponent lacks sufficient mating material, the game is declared a draw rather than a loss.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: If your flag falls and your time expires, you always lose the game even if your opponent has only a bare King left.

extra_socratic_questions: Why does a large open tournament use the Swiss pairing system instead of a single-elimination bracket or full round robin?
What verbal declaration must a player make before straightening an off-center piece on their turn to avoid a touch-move penalty?
Which clock hand must be used to press the tournament timer button after completing a move on the chessboard?
Under what condition does a player's Elo rating increase more for defeating an opponent than in a typical even-rated match?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Players must execute the move on the board first and then record it on the score sheet before or right after pressing the clock.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Under standard tournament rules, you should write your next move on your score sheet before moving the piece on the board.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Replaying wins as well as losses reveals missed tactics, defensive errors, and stronger candidate moves that improve future play.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Post-game review is only useful for games you lost, because winning a game proves every move you played was accurate.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Accurate move-by-move notation during play is essential so every position can be reconstructed without guesswork afterward.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: If your score sheet has an illegible or missing move, you can simply rely on memory weeks later during your counselor review.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Players must take their score sheets and move to a designated skittles or analysis room so ongoing tournament games are not disturbed.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Analyzing your tournament game aloud at the board immediately after finishing is fine even while adjacent games continue.

extra_socratic_questions: When should a player write down a move on the official score sheet during a tournament game under standard rules?
What happens to your post-game analysis with your counselor if an ambiguous or skipped move corrupts your score sheet?
Which critical turning points on a completed score sheet deserve the deepest evaluation when replaying a game afterward?
Why must both players verify and sign the recorded game result on the score sheets before leaving the tournament board?
